title: Cooking your food
supports: For foods that require thorough cooking, the centre should reach 70°C for 2 minutes or 75°C for 30 seconds. Poultry, pork and minced-meat dishes require thorough cooking. Reheat leftovers only once until steaming hot throughout.
scope: Safety rule only; not a tested formula or recipe endorsement.

title: How to chill, freeze and defrost food safely
supports: Keep the fridge at 0–5°C. Divide cooked food into smaller portions, cool promptly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours. General leftovers should be used within 48 hours or frozen. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours after fully thawing. Follow shorter product-specific instructions.
scope: Rice has a stricter rule; use fsa-rice-eggs. Freezer quality periods are not safety guarantees.

title: Home food fact checker
supports: Cool leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour; portion it instead of leaving it in the cooker or pan. Keep refrigerated rice no longer than 24 hours before use/reheating. Reheat only once until steaming throughout. Do not treat reheating as a way to rescue badly stored rice.
scope: The collection should apply this conservatively to cooked-rice dishes and rice-based leftovers; some foods need additional product-specific handling.

title: Why avoiding cross-contamination is important
supports: Do not wash raw meat, fish or poultry. Keep raw preparation separate from ready-to-eat food, clean boards and hands, and wash fruit and vegetables unless ready-to-eat labelling says otherwise.
scope: Apply in the relevant preparation steps, not solely in a global footer.

title: Handling flour and flour products safely
supports: Do not taste uncooked flour, dough or batter unless it is sold as ready to eat. Flour needs thorough cooking. Home heat-treatment methods cannot be assumed to eliminate every harmful bacterium.
scope: Important for noodles, dough, cake batter, dumplings and no-bake sweets; avoid raw-flour no-bake recipes.

title: Understanding food labelling: Vegan food labelling
supports: Vegan labelling concerns intentionally used animal ingredients and does not guarantee absence of cross-contamination. Check ingredient lists and precautionary allergen information. Do not infer milk safety from a vegan logo.
scope: No home recipe should promise zero cross-contact or certified free-from status.

title: Allergen guidance for food businesses
supports: Use the 14 regulated allergen categories as an ingredient-check reference: celery; gluten-containing cereals; crustaceans; eggs; fish; lupin; milk; molluscs; mustard; peanuts; sesame; soya; sulphur dioxide/sulphites; tree nuts. People can react to foods outside this list too.
scope: Reference taxonomy, not a claim that a private recipe website is a catering business or a complete allergy guarantee.

title: Milk allergy
publisher: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
supports: Milk-protein reactions are different from lactose intolerance. Lactose-free dairy milk is not a substitute when excluding milk protein.
scope: Supports ingredient exclusion only. Do not diagnose a person or reproduce their medical history.

title: Essential Plain White Flour
supports: A UK retail example labelled plain white flour, with wheat flour ingredients and an instruction to cook or bake before eating.
scope: Naming/product example only; no stock, price, postcode availability or milk cross-contact guarantee.

title: Flour
supports: Distinguishes plain flour, self-raising flour, strong white bread flour and wholemeal flour. Self-raising contains raising agents; strong flour has a different protein profile.
scope: Do not substitute these flour types blindly in noodles, dumplings and cakes.

title: Tesco Cornflour 250G
supports: UK retail naming example for cornflour sold for thickening gravies and sauces.
scope: Naming evidence only. Do not quote a current price or stock status. For a recipe specify white corn starch, not yellow cornmeal.

title: Tesco Shaoxing Rice Wine 150Ml
supports: UK listing for Shaoxing rice wine. This specific ingredient list includes wheat and the product contains alcohol.
scope: Brand formulations vary; recheck actual pack and allergens. Rice wine is not rice vinegar.

title: Ken Hom's curried chicken with peppers – ingredients
supports: This retailer-published recipe offers dry sherry as an alternative to Shaoxing rice wine.
scope: Supports a culinary swap option, not a universal chemical equivalence or alcohol-free result.

title: International vegetables
supports: UK retail naming examples include pak choi and choi sum.
scope: Category listing only, not assurance of local availability or current stock.

title: The Tofoo Co Naked Tofu Mini 180g
supports: A UK pre-pressed tofu product listing with water, soya beans and nigari; illustrates why tofu firmness and pressing instructions should be product-specific.
scope: Do not use extra-firm tofu as a texture-identical swap for silken tofu. Check current pack ingredients and storage.

title: Shuita Shanxi Superior Mature Vinegar, 5 Years Aged
supports: UK specialist retail example for Shanxi mature vinegar. Listed ingredients include sorghum and barley, illustrating that black vinegar may contain gluten.
scope: Do not claim every supermarket stocks it, quote a price, or assume all black vinegars have identical ingredients.

title: 十大晋菜名单公示 晋城人爱吃的有哪些？
publisher: 晋城市人民政府，转引山西晚报及省商务厅评审信息
supports: Officially hosted regional cuisine list supports named Jin dishes and noodle forms, including 过油肉、糖醋丸子、醋浇羊肉、葱烧台蘑 and several Shanxi noodles.
scope: Regional identity evidence only; it does not supply tested recipes or exact cooking proportions.

title: 并州饭店 – 老字号数字博物馆
publisher: 中华人民共和国商务部老字号数字博物馆
supports: Describes regional noodle and pastry traditions including 猫耳朵、包皮面、莜面栲栳栳、烧麦 and 一窝酥.
scope: Supports identity and naming, not recipe quantities or claims of authenticity for a substituted version.

title: 三个一号旅游公路沿线美食发布 高平里圪抓入选
supports: Regional food list includes 偏关油焖饭、临县合楞子、永和焖枣羊 and 运城石子饼.
